---
title: "What is a climate stress test?"
format: html
bibliography: references.bib
link-citations: true
---

A **climate stress test** examines how a system responds to deliberately varied climatic conditions,
with the purpose of finding combinations that cause unacceptable outcomes.
It extends sensitivity analysis by explicitly seeking the conditions under which a service, asset or
management strategy becomes vulnerable [@fowler2024].

For example, a reservoir assessment might explore how warming, reduced rainfall and prolonged dry spells
affect the ability to meet water demand.
A flood assessment might examine the rainfall changes under which a protection standard is exceeded.
The question is how far the system can be pushed, which processes cause failure, and whether an adaptation
measure changes those limits.

The experiment is often described as **scenario-neutral** because its climate perturbations are specified
independently of a selected set of climate-model projections.
It still uses scenarios: each tested combination represents a set of climatic conditions.
Separating the experiment from particular projections allows the same response analysis to be compared
with new climate information or different planning horizons [@prudhomme2010].
